title: The access-change record code, the matrix version label, the matrix screen, the agent identity source and the grant's service event are not in the sources, and two sources disagree on the group column of a role and on the right of the path
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E8-019); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P4 Access and administration v3.md (A2.30); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3.md (T3.1, T3.2, T6.1, T6.2, appendix T-A); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8.md; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3.md; _work/msr/context/P4.md
description: Six values of this key are not in the sources and two of them are conflicts. (1) The decision code that marks an access change in the local decision-record chain, the field-level shape of the letters before and after inside an entry, and the format of a matrix version label beyond the sample PM-2026.11 used by the sibling load story are not stated; the logical model fixes DF-DEC-003 as the code column and DF-REF-044 as the version column and no source gives either value. (2) The screen that carries the matrix is not named: the legacy screen table gives SCR-39 Rules and parameters and SCR-41 Delegation of authority, and neither is a matrix or an agent screen. (3) The store of an agent's service identity and of its allowed-action list is not declared for this service; NFR-051 and REQ-ACA-010 say agents run under service identities and are checked like people, the technical specification gives five system roles in the matrix, and no table of P4 holds an identity, so the grant can carry a reference only. (4) The source of a matrix version is not declared: permission.matrix_version exists (DF-REF-044) but no source says which act mints a new label, and the load path of RWB-P4-E1037-APP and RWB-P4-AD002-APP owns the versioned load while the legacy criterion asks a person to set access directly. (5) No source declares how a single grant reaches the services that cache permission data, and this story's pattern set and build dependencies carry the decision-record library and not the outbox platform story, so the access-policy event stays with the approval path. (6) The two conflicts: role.entra_group is a column of the role table in TSD P4 v3 T3.1 (DF-REF-039) and is explicitly not a Workbench column in FSD P4 v3 A2.30.3.2, which reads v_ace_iam_group instead; and the legacy permission table gives Rules and parameters C to RW-COE and A to RW-RISK while TSD P4 v3 T6.1 and API-P4-007 give the roles read Platform administration R and the administration write letters of the same area to RW-SECADM and RW-PLATADM.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E8-019 gives the story sentence, two generic ACs, a permission table (Rules and parameters C: RW-COE; A: RW-RISK), a data table naming decision_log_entry, rule_row, role and v_ace_iam_group with their field ranges, the two rule-version endpoints and the screens SCR-39 and SCR-41; FSD P4 v3 A2.30 gives VR-P4-030-1, BR-P4-030, the field catalog with role.role_class, role.default_scope, permission.capability_area and permission.letters, the note that v_ace_iam_group.entra_group is read from ACE and is not a Workbench column, the role table with the security administrator as primary, AC-P4-030-01 marked Written one epic ahead and the two exception criteria, and the requirement rows REQ-ACA-002, REQ-ACA-003 and REQ-ACA-010; TSD P4 v3 T3.1 gives role with DF-REF-039 entra_group and permission with DF-REF-044 matrix_version, T6.1 gives the matrix with the five system roles SY-CASEWF, SY-RULES, SY-DATALOAD, SY-OCR and SY-AGENT, and appendix T-A lists API-P4-007 GET /admin/roles with Platform administration R and no agent, grant or matrix-report path; the context pack rows for P4 name the four provided operations GET /admin/access-log, GET /admin/roles, GET /me/session and POST /admin/break-glass-grants, no event and one job JOB-18
proposed: Keep the matrix as rows of permission stamped with a matrix version, and let a single set mint the next label and supersede the version in force, so the person's act of the legacy criterion is a versioned change and not an edit in place; read the right from TSD P4 v3 T6.1 and API-P4-007 (Platform administration R on the three reads and C on the write) and record the legacy Rules and parameters letters as the rule-change right set of the same chapter; treat the five system roles of T6.1 as the agent roles and carry an agent reference on the grant instead of an identity column this service does not own; read the ACE groups through the read-only view and write nothing to role.entra_group; carry the record code, the entry shape and the version label format as open at D1 and settle them with the ledger owner and the load story; and leave the matrix screen to RWB-PLT-N001-CON with the access-policy event on the approval path of RWB-P4-E1037-APP. Keep the four paths on the access base, fixed by RWB-P4-E8019-CON.

title: The three new matrix operations, the schemas, the report columns and the CSV media type are not in the sources, and no source fixes the shape of a grant answer
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E8-019); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3.md (T3.1, T3.2, T6.1, appendix T-A); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P4 Access and administration v3.md (A2.30); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench API Specification v4.yaml; _work/msr/context/P4.md
description: The baseline fixes four operations of which one exists in the sources and three do not, and it fixes the shapes of six schemas that no source defines. (1) Only API-P4-007 GET /admin/roles is in TSD P4 v3 appendix T-A (Platform administration R); the agents read, the grant write and the matrix report exist in no appendix row and in no API Specification v4 path, so their paths, their request and answer documents, their rights and their error sets are settled here. (2) No source defines a Role, RolePermission, AgentRole, AccessMatrix, AccessMatrixRow or GrantRequest schema, a two-version answer, an agentRef field or a report column set; the field catalog of FSD P4 v3 A2.30 gives role.role_code, role.role_name, role.role_class, role.default_scope, permission.capability_area and permission.letters, and TSD P4 v3 T3.1 adds role.entra_group and permission.matrix_version. (3) The CSV media type, its header and the rule that the CSV and the JSON hold the same rows are a contract decision with no source. (4) The role_class, default_scope, capability_area and letters lists are named in TDS P4 v3 T3.1 and T3.2 and in FSD P4 v3 A2.30.3.2 as LOV-ROLE-CLASS, LOV-SCOPE, LOV-CAPABILITY and a string of C, R, U, D, A and the dash, and no source lists the fourteen capability areas, so the document enums them by LOV code. (5) The event declaration is one record message only, because no source gives a grant its own event and the service's access-policy name is declared by the load path.
evidence: TSD P4 v3 appendix T-A lists API-P4-004 to API-P4-021 with API-P4-007 GET /admin/roles as the only roles path and with no agent, grant or report path; API-P4-007 gives the purpose List roles with permissions and scope, the answer Role[], the errors 401, 403 and 503, the right Platform administration R and no idempotency; TSD P4 v3 T3.1 gives the two tables with their field ids and T3.2 gives the lists; FSD P4 v3 A2.30.3.2 gives the field catalog of the same feature and its note on v_ace_iam_group; the context pack rows for P4 name GET /admin/roles among the four provided operations and no event; the API Specification v4 extract carries no access-matrix path
proposed: Publish the four operations on the access base as API-P4-007 plus three: GET /admin/agents, PUT /admin/roles/{roleCode}/permissions and GET /admin/access-matrix; fix the six schemas with the fields of the two source tables and the report columns; enum the four closed sets by the LOV codes and never by a literal list; require both matrix versions on every answer of the write so a change can be read against what it replaced; declare the CSV media type with a fixed header and the rule that it holds the same rows as the JSON; declare the parameters read as consumed and the ACE group view as a read of this service's own connection; and declare the decision-record message only. Keep the load, the approval, the scope, the delegation and the guard out of this document.
